```{r Step 1, Dataset Set-up, include=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# Industry Harmonization: Inspect Source Classifications
# ============================================================
gss_all <- read_csv(here("01_tidydata", "GSS_Data_Cleaned", "gss_clean_2000_2024.csv"))
cps_wages_industry <- read_csv(here("01_tidydata", "IPUMS_CPS", "industry_wage_premium_2000_2025_n25.csv"))
cps_wages_base <- read_csv(here("01_tidydata", "IPUMS_CPS", "CPS_WagePremium_AnnualSample.csv"))
cps_wage_analysis <- read_csv(here("01_tidydata", "IPUMS_CPS", "cps_wage_analysis_2000_2024.csv"))
bls_benefits <- read_csv(here("01_tidydata","BLS_ECEC","ecec_benefits_industry_final_2004_2024.csv"))
bls_wages <- read_csv(here("01_tidydata","BLS_ECEC","ecec_wages_industry_annual_2004_2024.csv"))
jolts_turnover <- read_csv(here("01_tidydata", "BLS_JOLTS", "jolts_stability_industry_2000_2024.csv"))
qwi_earnings_volatility <- read_csv(here("01_tidydata", "QWI", "qwi_earnings_volatility_industry_annual_2001_2024.csv"))
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. GSS INDUS10
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_industries <- gss_all %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(indus10)
  ) %>%
  distinct(
    indus10
  ) %>%
  arrange(indus10)

gss_industries


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. CPS ASEC industries
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cps_industries <- cps_wages_industry %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(industry)
  ) %>%
  distinct(
    industry
  ) %>%
  arrange(industry)

cps_industries
```

```{r Step 2, Set-up Crosswalk, include=TRUE}
#Realized I needed to fix the crosswalk coding scheme for IPUMS
# ============================================================
# Diagnose CPS Industry Code Format
# ============================================================

# Examine the current industry codes
cps_wage_analysis %>%
  distinct(industry_clean) %>%
  arrange(industry_clean) %>%
  slice_head(n = 50)


# Check the current data type
class(cps_wage_analysis$industry_clean)


# Look at the smallest codes
cps_wage_analysis %>%
  distinct(industry_clean) %>%
  arrange(industry_clean) %>%
  slice_head(n = 20)


# Check number of digits in the current codes
cps_wage_analysis %>%
  distinct(industry_clean) %>%
  mutate(
    industry_digits = nchar(as.character(industry_clean))
  ) %>%
  count(industry_digits)


# Check how many codes are currently shorter than four digits
cps_wage_analysis %>%
  distinct(industry_clean) %>%
  mutate(
    industry_digits = nchar(as.character(industry_clean))
  ) %>%
  filter(industry_digits < 4) %>%
  arrange(industry_clean)


cps_wage_analysis <- cps_wage_analysis %>% mutate( industry_clean = sprintf( "%04d", as.integer(industry_clean) ) )

cps_wage_analysis %>% filter(!is.na(industry_clean)) %>% summarise( n_codes = n_distinct(industry_clean), min_digits = min(nchar(industry_clean)), max_digits = max(nchar(industry_clean)) )

# ============================================================
# Standardize CPS industry codes
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Add four-digit character industry_code to microdata
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cps_wage_analysis <- cps_wage_analysis %>%
  mutate(
    industry_code = sprintf(
      "%04d",
      as.integer(industry_clean)
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Add four-digit character industry_code to
#    industry-level dataset
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cps_wages_industry <- cps_wages_industry %>%
  mutate(
    industry_code = sprintf(
      "%04d",
      as.integer(industry)
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Check the new variables
# ------------------------------------------------------------

class(cps_wage_analysis$industry_code)

class(cps_wages_industry$industry_code)


# Check that all non-missing codes are four digits

cps_wage_analysis %>%
  filter(!is.na(industry_code)) %>%
  summarise(
    n_industries = n_distinct(industry_code),
    min_digits = min(nchar(industry_code)),
    max_digits = max(nchar(industry_code))
  )

cps_wages_industry %>%
  filter(!is.na(industry_code)) %>%
  summarise(
    n_industries = n_distinct(industry_code),
    min_digits = min(nchar(industry_code)),
    max_digits = max(nchar(industry_code))
  )


# ============================================================
# Compare industry coverage
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Industries in the microdata but not the
#    industry-level dataset
# ------------------------------------------------------------

missing_cps_industries <- cps_wage_analysis %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(industry_code)
  ) %>%
  distinct(
    industry_code
  ) %>%
  anti_join(
    cps_wages_industry %>%
      filter(!is.na(industry_code)) %>%
      distinct(industry_code),
    by = "industry_code"
  ) %>%
  arrange(industry_code)

missing_cps_industries


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Industries in the industry-level dataset but not
#    the microdata
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cps_wages_industry %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(industry_code)
  ) %>%
  distinct(
    industry_code
  ) %>%
  anti_join(
    cps_wage_analysis %>%
      filter(!is.na(industry_code)) %>%
      distinct(industry_code),
    by = "industry_code"
  ) %>%
  arrange(industry_code)


# ============================================================
# Diagnose the missing industries
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Number of microdata observations
# ------------------------------------------------------------

missing_cps_industries %>%
  left_join(
    cps_wage_analysis %>%
      filter(!is.na(industry_code)) %>%
      count(
        industry_code,
        name = "microdata_n"
      ),
    by = "industry_code"
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    microdata_n,
    industry_code
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Weighted sample size
# ------------------------------------------------------------

missing_cps_industries %>%
  left_join(
    cps_wage_analysis %>%
      filter(!is.na(industry_code)) %>%
      group_by(industry_code) %>%
      summarise(
        microdata_n = n(),
        weighted_n =
          sum(
            asecwt_clean,
            na.rm = TRUE
          ),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = "industry_code"
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    weighted_n,
    industry_code
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Year coverage
# ------------------------------------------------------------

missing_cps_industries %>%
  left_join(
    cps_wage_analysis %>%
      filter(!is.na(industry_code)) %>%
      group_by(industry_code) %>%
      summarise(
        first_year = min(year),
        last_year = max(year),
        n_years = n_distinct(year),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = "industry_code"
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    industry_code
  )

# ============================================================
# Verify CPS industry-year reliability filter
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Reconstruct industry-year sample sizes from microdata
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cps_industry_year_counts <- cps_wage_analysis %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(industry_code),
    !is.na(year)
  ) %>%
  count(
    year,
    industry_code,
    name = "microdata_n"
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Identify industry-year cells represented in the
#    industry-level wage dataset
# ------------------------------------------------------------

retained_industry_years <- cps_wages_industry %>%
  distinct(
    year,
    industry_code
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Join the microdata counts to retained cells
# ------------------------------------------------------------

retained_cell_check <- retained_industry_years %>%
  left_join(
    cps_industry_year_counts,
    by = c("year", "industry_code")
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Check whether ANY retained cell has fewer than 25
#    observations
# ------------------------------------------------------------

retained_cell_check %>%
  filter(
    microdata_n < 25
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    microdata_n,
    year,
    industry_code
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Summarize the retained cells
# ------------------------------------------------------------

retained_cell_check %>%
  summarise(
    n_industry_years = n(),
    min_n = min(microdata_n, na.rm = TRUE),
    p01_n = quantile(microdata_n, 0.01, na.rm = TRUE),
    p05_n = quantile(microdata_n, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_n = median(microdata_n, na.rm = TRUE),
    p95_n = quantile(microdata_n, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_n = max(microdata_n, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_below_25 = sum(microdata_n < 25, na.rm = TRUE)
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Check the opposite:
#    Which microdata industry-year cells meet n >= 25
#    but are NOT in cps_wages_industry?
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cps_industry_year_counts %>%
  filter(
    microdata_n >= 25
  ) %>%
  anti_join(
    retained_industry_years,
    by = c("year", "industry_code")
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    year,
    industry_code
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Final summary of the relationship
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cps_industry_year_counts %>%
  mutate(
    meets_threshold = microdata_n >= 25,
    retained_in_wage_data =
      paste(year, industry_code) %in%
      paste(
        retained_industry_years$year,
        retained_industry_years$industry_code
      )
  ) %>%
  count(
    meets_threshold,
    retained_in_wage_data
  )


#Resave Microdata
write_csv(
  cps_wage_analysis,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "IPUMS_CPS",
    "cps_wage_analysis_2000_2024.csv"
  )
)

#Resave Industry Level Data
write_csv(
  cps_wages_industry,
  here("01_tidydata", "IPUMS_CPS", "cps_wages_industry_2000_2024_n25.csv")
)
```

```{r Step 5: Building the Census Crosswalk, include=TRUE}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create four-digit version of GSS INDUS10
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_all <- gss_all %>%
  mutate(
    industry_code = sprintf("%04d", as.integer(indus10))
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Map 2010 Census / NAICS 2007 industry codes
#    into our 17 BLS-compatible industry categories
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_all <- gss_all %>%
  mutate(
    industry_bls17 = case_when(

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Natural resources
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      as.integer(industry_code) >= 170 &
        as.integer(industry_code) <= 290 ~
        "Agriculture, forestry, fishing, and hunting",

      as.integer(industry_code) >= 370 &
        as.integer(industry_code) <= 490 ~
        "Mining",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Utilities
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      as.integer(industry_code) >= 570 &
        as.integer(industry_code) <= 690 ~
        "Utilities",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Construction
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      as.integer(industry_code) == 770 ~
        "Construction",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Manufacturing
      # 1070–2390 = nondurable
      # 2470–3990 = durable
      # Combined because our BLS measures use Manufacturing
      # as the common industry.
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      as.integer(industry_code) >= 1070 &
        as.integer(industry_code) <= 3990 ~
        "Manufacturing",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Trade
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      as.integer(industry_code) >= 4070 &
        as.integer(industry_code) <= 4590 ~
        "Wholesale trade",

      as.integer(industry_code) >= 4670 &
        as.integer(industry_code) <= 5790 ~
        "Retail trade",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Transportation and warehousing
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      as.integer(industry_code) >= 6070 &
        as.integer(industry_code) <= 6390 ~
        "Transportation and warehousing",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Information
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      as.integer(industry_code) >= 6470 &
        as.integer(industry_code) <= 6780 ~
        "Information",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Finance and insurance
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      as.integer(industry_code) >= 6870 &
        as.integer(industry_code) <= 7190 ~
        "Finance and insurance",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Professional / scientific / technical
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      as.integer(industry_code) >= 7270 &
        as.integer(industry_code) <= 7490 ~
        "Professional, scientific, and technical services",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Administrative/support/waste management
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      as.integer(industry_code) >= 7570 &
        as.integer(industry_code) <= 7790 ~
        "Administrative and support and waste management",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Education
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      as.integer(industry_code) >= 7860 &
        as.integer(industry_code) <= 7960 ~
        "Educational services",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Health care and social assistance
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      as.integer(industry_code) >= 7970 &
        as.integer(industry_code) <= 8550 ~
        "Health care and social assistance",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Leisure and hospitality
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      as.integer(industry_code) >= 8560 &
        as.integer(industry_code) <= 8690 ~
        "Leisure and hospitality",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Other services
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      as.integer(industry_code) >= 8770 &
        as.integer(industry_code) <= 9290 ~
        "Other services",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Public administration
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      as.integer(industry_code) >= 9370 &
        as.integer(industry_code) <= 9590 ~
        "Public administration",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Everything else remains NA for inspection
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Inspect the resulting distribution
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_all %>%
  count(industry_bls17, sort = TRUE)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Check which observed INDUS10 codes remain unmapped
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_unmapped_industry <- gss_all %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(industry_code),
    is.na(industry_bls17)
  ) %>%
  count(industry_code, sort = TRUE)

gss_unmapped_industry


gss_all <- gss_all %>%
  mutate(
    industry_bls17 = case_when(
      
      # Military → Public administration
      industry_code %in% c(
        "9670", "9680", "9690",
        "9770", "9780", "9790", "9870"
      ) ~ "Public administration",
      
      # GSS non-substantive / missing code
      industry_code == "00NA" ~ NA_character_,
      
      # Keep all previously assigned categories
      TRUE ~ industry_bls17
    )
  )

# Check remaining unmapped codes
gss_all %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(industry_code),
    is.na(industry_bls17)
  ) %>%
  count(industry_code, sort = TRUE)


gss_all <- gss_all %>%
  mutate(
    industry_code = if_else(
      is.na(suppressWarnings(as.integer(indus10))),
      NA_character_,
      sprintf("%04d", as.integer(indus10))
    )
  )

gss_all %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(industry_code),
    is.na(industry_bls17)
  ) %>%
  count(industry_code, sort = TRUE)



gss_all <- gss_all %>%
  mutate(
    indus10_num = suppressWarnings(as.integer(indus10)),

    industry_bls17 = case_when(

      # Construction
      indus10_num == 770 ~
        "Construction",

      # Manufacturing
      indus10_num >= 1070 &
        indus10_num <= 3990 ~
        "Manufacturing",

      # Wholesale
      indus10_num >= 4070 &
        indus10_num <= 4590 ~
        "Wholesale trade",

      # Retail
      indus10_num >= 4670 &
        indus10_num <= 5790 ~
        "Retail trade",

      # Transportation and warehousing
      indus10_num >= 6070 &
        indus10_num <= 6390 ~
        "Transportation and warehousing",

      # Information
      indus10_num >= 6470 &
        indus10_num <= 6780 ~
        "Information",

      # Finance and insurance
      indus10_num >= 6870 &
        indus10_num <= 6990 ~
        "Finance and insurance",

      # Real estate and rental/leasing
      indus10_num >= 7070 &
        indus10_num <= 7190 ~
        "Real estate and rental and leasing",

      # Professional/scientific/technical
      indus10_num >= 7270 &
        indus10_num <= 7490 ~
        "Professional, scientific, and technical services",

      # Administrative/support/waste
      indus10_num >= 7570 &
        indus10_num <= 7790 ~
        "Administrative and support and waste management",

      # Educational services
      indus10_num >= 7860 &
        indus10_num <= 7890 ~
        "Educational services",

      # Health care/social assistance
      indus10_num >= 7970 &
        indus10_num <= 8470 ~
        "Health care and social assistance",

      # Leisure and hospitality
      indus10_num >= 8560 &
        indus10_num <= 8590 ~
        "Leisure and hospitality",

      # Accommodation and food services
      indus10_num >= 8660 &
        indus10_num <= 8690 ~
        "Accommodation and food services",

      # Other services
      indus10_num >= 8770 &
        indus10_num <= 9290 ~
        "Other services",

      # Agriculture, mining, utilities, public administration:
      # no corresponding ECEC industry series
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Check the resulting industry distribution
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_all %>%
  count(industry_bls17, sort = TRUE)

# Check that every substantive INDUS10 code was classified
gss_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(indus10_num)) %>%
  count(industry_bls17, sort = TRUE)

# Save
write_csv(
  gss_all,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "gss_clean_2000_2024_with_industry_bls17.csv"
  )
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Check how much of the GSS sample is successfully mapped
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_all %>%
  summarise(
    n_total = n(),
    n_industry_nonmissing = sum(!is.na(indus10)),
    n_mapped = sum(!is.na(industry_bls17)),
    n_unmapped = sum(
      !is.na(indus10) &
      is.na(industry_bls17)
    ),
    pct_mapped_among_industry =
      100 * n_mapped / n_industry_nonmissing
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Check the number of unique source codes in each category
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(industry_bls17)) %>%
  group_by(industry_bls17) %>%
  summarise(
    n_indus10_codes = n_distinct(industry_code),
    n_respondents = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(industry_bls17)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Save the GSS data with the harmonized industry variable
# ------------------------------------------------------------

write_csv(
  gss_all,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "gss_clean_2000_2024_with_industry_bls17.csv"
  )
)
```

```{r Step 7: Final Merge Construction - Standardization, include=TRUE}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# STANDARDIZE INDUSTRY NAMES ACROSS SOURCES
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# ECEC benefits
bls_benefits_merge <- bls_benefits %>%
  mutate(
    industry_bls17 = case_when(
      industry == "Other services except public administration" ~
        "Other services",
      industry == "Administrative and support and waste management and remediation services" ~
        "Administrative and support and waste management",
      TRUE ~ industry
    )
  )

# ECEC wages
bls_wages_merge <- bls_wages %>%
  mutate(
    industry_bls17 = case_when(
      industry == "Other services except public administration" ~
        "Other services",
      industry == "Administrative and support and waste management and remediation services" ~
        "Administrative and support and waste management",
      TRUE ~ industry
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# JOLTS → COMMON INDUSTRY KEY
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jolts_merge <- jolts_turnover %>%
  mutate(
    industry_bls17 = case_when(

      industry == "Construction" ~
        "Construction",

      industry == "Manufacturing" ~
        "Manufacturing",

      industry == "Durable goods manufacturing" ~
        "Manufacturing",

      industry == "Nondurable goods manufacturing" ~
        "Manufacturing",

      industry == "Wholesale trade" ~
        "Wholesale trade",

      industry == "Retail trade" ~
        "Retail trade",

      industry == "Real estate and rental and leasing" ~
        "Real estate and rental and leasing",

      industry == "Health care and social assistance" ~
        "Health care and social assistance",

      industry == "Private educational services" ~
        "Educational services",

      industry == "Accommodation and food services" ~
        "Accommodation and food services",

      industry == "Leisure and hospitality" ~
        "Leisure and hospitality",

      # Arts/entertainment/recreation is a component of
      # Leisure and hospitality, so this is defensible.
      industry == "Arts, entertainment, and recreation" ~
        "Leisure and hospitality",

      # These JOLTS aggregates do NOT map cleanly to one
      # GSS industry, so leave them unmatched.
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# QWI → COMMON INDUSTRY KEY
# ------------------------------------------------------------

qwi_merge <- qwi_earnings_volatility %>%
  mutate(
    industry_bls17 = case_when(

      industry == "23" ~
        "Construction",

      industry == "31-33" ~
        "Manufacturing",

      industry == "42" ~
        "Wholesale trade",

      industry == "44-45" ~
        "Retail trade",

      industry == "48-49" ~
        "Transportation and warehousing",

      industry == "51" ~
        "Information",

# ------------------------------------------------------------

cps_wages_industry_merge <- cps_wages_industry_merge %>%
  mutate(
    industry_num = as.integer(industry_code),

    industry_common = case_when(

      # ========================================================
      # 2000-2002: 1990 Census industry classification
      # ========================================================

      year <= 2002 & industry_num == 60 ~
        "Construction",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Manufacturing
      # Food, textiles, paper, chemicals, petroleum, leather,
      # wood, furniture, minerals, metals, machinery, electronics,
      # transportation equipment, miscellaneous manufacturing
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      year <= 2002 &
        industry_num >= 100 &
        industry_num <= 392 ~
        "Manufacturing",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Wholesale trade
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      year <= 2002 &
        industry_num >= 500 &
        industry_num <= 571 ~
        "Wholesale trade",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Retail trade
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      year <= 2002 &
        industry_num >= 580 &
        industry_num <= 691 ~
        "Retail trade",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Transportation and warehousing
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      year <= 2002 &
        industry_num >= 400 &
        industry_num <= 432 ~
        "Transportation and warehousing",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Information
      # Broadcasting, telephone, telegraph
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      year <= 2002 &
        industry_num >= 440 &
        industry_num <= 442 ~
        "Information",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Utilities
      # No corresponding GSS/BLS common category, so leave NA.
      # --------------------------------------------------------

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Finance and insurance
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      year <= 2002 &
        industry_num >= 700 &
        industry_num <= 711 ~
        "Finance and insurance",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Real estate
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      year <= 2002 &
        industry_num == 712 ~
        "Real estate and rental and leasing",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Professional, scientific, and technical services
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      year <= 2002 &
        industry_num %in% c(
          721, 730, 732,
          741,
          841,
          882, 890, 891, 892, 893
        ) ~
        "Professional, scientific, and technical services",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Administrative/support/waste
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      year <= 2002 &
        industry_num %in% c(
          722, 731, 740, 742,
          750, 751, 752
        ) ~
        "Administrative and support and waste management",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Educational services
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      year <= 2002 &
        industry_num >= 842 &
        industry_num <= 862 ~
        "Educational services",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Health care and social assistance
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      year <= 2002 &
        industry_num >= 812 &
        industry_num <= 840 ~
        "Health care and social assistance",

      # Social services
      year <= 2002 &
        industry_num %in% c(870, 871) ~
        "Health care and social assistance",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Leisure and hospitality
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      year <= 2002 &
        industry_num %in% c(
          800, 801, 802, 810,
          762, 770
        ) ~
        "Leisure and hospitality",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Other services
      # --------------------------------------------------------
      year <= 2002 &
        industry_num %in% c(
          771, 772, 780, 781, 782,
          790, 791,
          872, 873,
          880, 881
        ) ~
        "Other services",

      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Everything else remains NA:
      # agriculture, mining, utilities, public administration,
      # military, etc.
      # --------------------------------------------------------

      TRUE ~ industry_common
    )
  )
```

```{r Step 9, Rebuild the Merge One More Time, include=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# REBUILD PRIMARY INDUSTRY-YEAR JOB QUALITY PANEL
# ============================================================
#
# Primary JQI will NOT include JOLTS employment stability.
#
# JOLTS is retained in the panel as a supplementary measure.
# Industries without JOLTS coverage remain in the dataset with
# NA for layoffs_discharge_rate and stability_reverse.
#
# ============================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. DEFINE THE COMMON 14-INDUSTRY UNIVERSE
# ------------------------------------------------------------

common_industries <- c(
  "Construction",
  "Manufacturing",
  "Wholesale trade",
  "Retail trade",
  "Transportation and warehousing",
  "Information",
  "Finance and insurance",
  "Real estate and rental and leasing",
  "Professional, scientific, and technical services",
  "Administrative and support and waste management",
  "Educational services",
  "Health care and social assistance",
  "Leisure and hospitality",
  "Other services"
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. DEFINE THE COMPLETE INDUSTRY-YEAR SKELETON
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# This guarantees 14 industries x 25 years = 350 rows.
#
# Any source measure that does not exist for a given
# industry-year will be NA rather than causing the row
# to disappear.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_year_skeleton <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  year = 2000:2024,
  industry_common = common_industries
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. CPS WAGE PREMIUM
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cps_wage_merge <- cps_wages_industry_merge %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(industry_common),
    industry_common %in% common_industries,
    !is.na(industry_wage_premium)
  ) %>%
  group_by(year, industry_common) %>%
  summarise(
    wage_premium = weighted.mean(
      industry_wage_premium,
      w = industry_year_n,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    wage_premium_pct = weighted.mean(
      industry_wage_premium_pct,
      w = industry_year_n,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    cps_industry_n = sum(
      industry_year_n,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    n_cps_industries = n_distinct(industry_code),

    .groups = "drop"
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. ECEC WAGES
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Already cleaned above as ecec_wage_merge.
#


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. ECEC BENEFITS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Already cleaned above as ecec_benefit_merge.
#


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. QWI EARNINGS VOLATILITY
# ------------------------------------------------------------

qwi_volatility_merge <- qwi_merge %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(industry_bls17),
    industry_bls17 %in% common_industries,
    !is.na(earnings_volatility)
  ) %>%
  select(
    year,
    industry_bls17,
    earnings_volatility
  ) %>%
  rename(
    industry_common = industry_bls17
  ) %>%
  group_by(year, industry_common) %>%
  summarise(
    earnings_volatility = mean(
      earnings_volatility,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. JOLTS STABILITY
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# IMPORTANT:
# This is NOT used to determine which rows exist in the
# primary panel.
#
# It is simply joined onto the complete 14-industry panel.
#
# Industries without JOLTS coverage will therefore have
# NA for layoffs_discharge_rate and stability_reverse.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jolts_stability_merge <- jolts_merge %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(industry_bls17)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !(industry_bls17 == "Manufacturing" &
        industry != "Manufacturing"),
    !(industry_bls17 == "Leisure and hospitality" &
        industry != "Leisure and hospitality")
  ) %>%
  select(
    year,
    industry_bls17,
    layoffs_discharge_rate
  ) %>%
  rename(
    industry_common = industry_bls17
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    stability_reverse = -layoffs_discharge_rate
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. MERGE ALL MEASURES ONTO THE COMPLETE SKELETON
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_year_job_quality <- industry_year_skeleton %>%

  # CPS compensation
  left_join(
    cps_wage_merge,
    by = c("year", "industry_common")
  ) %>%

  # ECEC wages
  left_join(
    ecec_wage_merge,
    by = c("year", "industry_common")
  ) %>%

  # ECEC benefits
  left_join(
    ecec_benefit_merge,
    by = c("year", "industry_common")
  ) %>%

  # QWI earnings volatility
  left_join(
    qwi_volatility_merge,
    by = c("year", "industry_common")
  ) %>%

  # JOLTS stability — supplementary only
  left_join(
    jolts_stability_merge,
    by = c("year", "industry_common")
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    industry_common,
    year
  )


# ============================================================
# 9. CHECK FOR DUPLICATES
# ============================================================

industry_year_job_quality %>%
  count(
    year,
    industry_common
  ) %>%
  filter(n > 1)


# ============================================================
# 10. CHECK OVERALL STRUCTURE
# ============================================================

industry_year_job_quality %>%
  summarise(
    n_rows = n(),
    n_industries = n_distinct(industry_common),
    first_year = min(year, na.rm = TRUE),
    last_year = max(year, na.rm = TRUE)
  )


# Expected:
# n_rows = 350
# n_industries = 14
# first_year = 2000
# last_year = 2024


# ============================================================
# 11. CHECK COVERAGE OF EACH MEASURE
# ============================================================

industry_year_job_quality %>%
  summarise(
    n_rows = n(),

    wage_premium_n =
      sum(!is.na(wage_premium)),

    ecec_wage_n =
      sum(!is.na(wage_cost_per_hour)),

    benefits_nonrequired_n =
      sum(!is.na(benefits_nonrequired)),

    layoffs_discharge_rate_n =
      sum(!is.na(layoffs_discharge_rate)),

    earnings_volatility_n =
      sum(!is.na(earnings_volatility))
  )


# ============================================================
# 12. CHECK JOLTS COVERAGE SPECIFICALLY
# ============================================================

jolts_coverage_check <- industry_year_job_quality %>%
  group_by(industry_common) %>%
  summarise(
    n_years = n(),

    jolts_n =
      sum(!is.na(layoffs_discharge_rate)),

    jolts_missing =
      sum(is.na(layoffs_discharge_rate)),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(industry_common)

jolts_coverage_check


# ============================================================
# 13. CHECK THAT JOLTS DOES NOT DETERMINE ROW RETENTION
# ============================================================

industry_year_job_quality %>%
  count(
    industry_common,
    name = "n_rows"
  )


# Every industry should have:
# n_rows = 25


# ============================================================
# 14. CHECK THE SIX INDUSTRIES WITHOUT JOLTS COVERAGE
# ============================================================

industry_year_job_quality %>%
  group_by(industry_common) %>%
  summarise(
    jolts_coverage = mean(
      !is.na(layoffs_discharge_rate)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(jolts_coverage, industry_common)



# ============================================================
# 15. SAVE THE CLEAN EXTERNAL PANEL
# ============================================================

saveRDS(
  industry_year_job_quality,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "industry_year_job_quality_2000_2024.rds"
  )
)

write_csv(
  industry_year_job_quality,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "industry_year_job_quality_2000_2024.csv"
  )
)

industry_year_job_quality %>%
  group_by(industry_common) %>%
  summarise(
    n_years = n(),
    jolts_n = sum(!is.na(layoffs_discharge_rate)),
    jolts_missing = sum(is.na(layoffs_discharge_rate))
  )
```

```{r Step 10, Now We Merge to the Survey Data, include=TRUE}
common_industries <- c(
  "Construction",
  "Manufacturing",
  "Wholesale trade",
  "Retail trade",
  "Transportation and warehousing",
  "Information",
  "Finance and insurance",
  "Real estate and rental and leasing",
  "Professional, scientific, and technical services",
  "Administrative and support and waste management",
  "Educational services",
  "Health care and social assistance",
  "Leisure and hospitality",
  "Other services"
)

gss_all <- gss_all %>%
  mutate(
    indus10_num = suppressWarnings(as.integer(indus10)),
    
    industry_bls17 = case_when(
      indus10_num == 770 ~ "Construction",
      indus10_num >= 1070 & indus10_num <= 3990 ~ "Manufacturing",
      indus10_num >= 4070 & indus10_num <= 4590 ~ "Wholesale trade",
      indus10_num >= 4670 & indus10_num <= 5790 ~ "Retail trade",
      indus10_num >= 6070 & indus10_num <= 6390 ~ "Transportation and warehousing",
      indus10_num >= 6470 & indus10_num <= 6780 ~ "Information",
      indus10_num >= 6870 & indus10_num <= 6990 ~ "Finance and insurance",
      indus10_num >= 7070 & indus10_num <= 7190 ~ "Real estate and rental and leasing",
      indus10_num >= 7270 & indus10_num <= 7490 ~ "Professional, scientific, and technical services",
      indus10_num >= 7570 & indus10_num <= 7790 ~ "Administrative and support and waste management",
      indus10_num >= 7860 & indus10_num <= 7890 ~ "Educational services",
      indus10_num >= 7970 & indus10_num <= 8470 ~ "Health care and social assistance",
      indus10_num >= 8560 & indus10_num <= 8590 ~ "Leisure and hospitality",
      indus10_num >= 8660 & indus10_num <= 8690 ~ "Accommodation and food services",
      indus10_num >= 8770 & indus10_num <= 9290 ~ "Other services",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    
    industry_common = case_when(
      industry_bls17 %in% c(
        "Leisure and hospitality",
        "Accommodation and food services"
      ) ~ "Leisure and hospitality",
      TRUE ~ industry_bls17
    )
  )

job_quality_primary <- industry_year_job_quality %>%
  mutate(
    z_wage_premium = as.numeric(scale(wage_premium)),
    z_ecec_wage = as.numeric(scale(wage_cost_per_hour)),
    z_benefits = as.numeric(scale(benefits_nonrequired)),
    z_earnings_stability = as.numeric(
      scale(-earnings_volatility)
    ),
    
    compensation = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        z_wage_premium,
        z_ecec_wage
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    ),
    
    benefits = z_benefits,
    
    earnings_stability = z_earnings_stability,
    
    jqi_primary = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        compensation,
        benefits,
        earnings_stability
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    jqi_primary_z = as.numeric(scale(jqi_primary))
  )

job_quality_primary %>%
  summarise(
    n_rows = n(),
    n_industries = n_distinct(industry_common),
    first_year = min(year),
    last_year = max(year),
    primary_jqi_n = sum(!is.na(jqi_primary)),
    primary_jqi_mean = mean(jqi_primary, na.rm = TRUE),
    primary_jqi_sd = sd(jqi_primary, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

job_quality_primary %>%
  count(year, industry_common) %>%
  filter(n > 1)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Merge onto GSS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
gss_job_quality_primary <- gss_all %>%
  left_join(
    job_quality_primary %>%
      select(
        year,
        industry_common,
        
        # Compensation
        wage_premium,
        wage_premium_pct,
        wage_cost_per_hour,
        compensation,
        
        # Benefits
        benefits_nonrequired,
        benefits_total,
        benefits_paid_leave,
        benefits_insurance,
        benefits_retirement,
        benefits,
        
        # Earnings stability
        earnings_volatility,
        earnings_stability,
        
        # Primary composite
        jqi_primary,
        jqi_primary_z,
        
        # Supplementary JOLTS measure
        layoffs_discharge_rate,
        stability_reverse
      ),
    by = c("year", "industry_common")
  )


gss_job_quality_primary %>%
  summarise(
    n_gss = n(),
    n_industry_missing = sum(is.na(industry_common)),
    n_industry_match = sum(
      !is.na(industry_common) &
      !is.na(wage_premium)
    ),
    pct_industry_match = mean(
      !is.na(industry_common) &
      !is.na(wage_premium)
    ) * 100
  )

gss_job_quality_primary %>%
  summarise(
    n_total = n(),
    
    wage_premium_n = sum(!is.na(wage_premium)),
    ecec_wage_n = sum(!is.na(wage_cost_per_hour)),
    benefits_n = sum(!is.na(benefits_nonrequired)),
    earnings_stability_n = sum(!is.na(earnings_stability)),
    
    primary_jqi_n = sum(!is.na(jqi_primary)),
    
    jolts_n = sum(!is.na(layoffs_discharge_rate))
  )

gss_job_quality_primary %>%
  count(year, name = "n_gss") %>%
  left_join(
    gss_job_quality_primary %>%
      group_by(year) %>%
      summarise(
        primary_jqi_n = sum(!is.na(jqi_primary)),
        primary_jqi_pct = mean(!is.na(jqi_primary)) * 100,
        jolts_n = sum(!is.na(layoffs_discharge_rate)),
        jolts_pct = mean(!is.na(layoffs_discharge_rate)) * 100,
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = "year"
  )
# ============================================================
# SAVE MERGED DATA
# ============================================================

saveRDS(
  gss_job_quality_primary,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "gss_job_quality_primary_2000_2024.rds"
  )
)

write_csv(
  gss_job_quality_primary,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "GSS_Data_Cleaned",
    "gss_job_quality_primary_2000_2024.csv"
  )
)
```
